title: Quiet Errands
tagline: A neighbour is missing, and the trail starts with three small jobs.
opening: Someone from the nearest village vanished three nights ago, and nobody will say why. The only clues are small ones. Follow them before the trail goes cold.
ending: You found who was behind it and stopped them. The village sleeps safely tonight, and they know who to thank.

steps.tell: The missing neighbour was last seen gathering supplies in {area}. Collect what they left behind. It may show where they went.
Their trail leads to a place in {area}. Go and look. Something happened there that the villagers are afraid to talk about.
Whatever took them is still in {area}, and it will take someone else next. Defeat it now.

title: The Long Road
tagline: The only trade road is cut. Reopen it before winter.
opening: The trade road has been cut for weeks, and the villages at the far end are running out of food. Someone has to clear it, stop by stop, before winter closes in.
ending: The road is open again. Carts are already rolling, and the far villages will eat this winter because of you.

steps.tell: The first stop is {area}. Nobody has come back from there in weeks. Find out why.
Raiders took over the road in {area}. Defeat them, or no cart will ever get through.
The road crews need supplies to rebuild it. Gather them in {area}.
The last blocked stretch is in {area}, where the road crews buried their tools. Find them so the road can be finished.

title: The Great Hunt
tagline: Something is driving the beasts mad. Trace it to its source.
opening: Beasts that never used to attack villages are suddenly raiding them, as if something is driving them. If nobody finds the cause, the next raid reaches a town.
ending: The source is destroyed and the beasts are calm again. The villages are safe, and the hunters will remember what you did.

steps.tell: The raids start here in {area}. Defeat the beasts and watch which way the survivors run.
The survivors fled to {area} and are angrier there. Stop them before they reach the villages.
Whatever is driving them is close, in {area}. Defeat the beasts guarding it.
Their trail ends in {area}. Go there and end this.

title: A Harvest Against the Dark
tagline: The winter food is still in the fields, and something is hunting the gatherers.
opening: The villages have no winter food unless the last crops are gathered this week, but something has started hunting the gatherers. Bring the harvest in, and protect it.
ending: The harvest is in, and the villages will have enough to last until spring.

steps.tell: Start in {area}. The nearest crops are there. Gather as much as you can carry.
Something is stalking the gatherers in {area}. Defeat it before it kills someone.
There is more food in {area}, past where the stalker hid. Gather it and finish the harvest.

title: The Lost Relics
tagline: Three old treasures could pay for a village to rebuild. Find them.
opening: A village burned down last spring and cannot afford to rebuild. Three old treasures are hidden in three different lands, and together they could pay for everything. Find them before treasure hunters do.
ending: All three treasures are found, and the village will be rebuilt.

steps.tell: The first treasure is hidden in {area}. Search the area for it.
The second treasure is in {area}. It is buried deeper, so search carefully.
The third and last treasure is in {area}. Find it before anyone else does.

title: Pilgrimage to the Far Shrine
tagline: A dying elder wants to see the far shrine. Clear the way for the pilgrimage.
opening: The village elder is dying and has one wish: to see the far shrine once more. The route is long and dangerous. Go ahead of the pilgrims and make it safe for them.
ending: The shrine is open and the way is safe. The elder will make the trip, thanks to you.

steps.tell: The pilgrimage starts at {area}. Go there and make sure the way is passable.
Next is {area}. It is a longer walk than it looks, so scout it before the pilgrims arrive.
Then {area}. Other scouts turned back here. Do not.
Enemies guard the shrine in {area}. Defeat them so the pilgrims can reach it.

title: The Siege of the Frontier
tagline: Raiders are besieging the frontier. Break the siege before supplies run out.
opening: Raiders have besieged the frontier settlement, and its food will last only days. Break the siege, then find out who is leading the raiders.
ending: The siege is broken and the raiders scattered. The settlement is free, and they will not forget who saved them.

steps.tell: The first raiding party is in {area}. Defeat it before it reaches the settlement.
The settlement is running out of food. Gather supplies in {area} and bring them back.
A second raiding party is forming in {area}. Strike before it is ready.
The raid leaders are in {area}. Defeat them and the raiders will break.
The leaders dropped something they came here for. Search {area} for it so they cannot come back for it.

title: Beyond the Edge of the Map
tagline: Map the farthest lands before the cartographers give up on them.
opening: The cartographers say the farthest lands are empty, and will stop paying for expeditions unless someone brings proof. Travel to the edge of the map and bring back evidence.
ending: You reached the farthest land and came back with proof. The expedition will be funded again.

steps.tell: Go to {area}, where the known map begins to thin out.
Gather plants that only grow in {area}. They are the proof the cartographers want.
Something lives in {area} and does not welcome visitors. Defeat it.
Search the edge of {area} for a marker left by the first explorers. It proves they were here.

title: The Hollow Crown
tagline: Thieves stole the royal crown. Follow them and bring it back.
opening: The royal crown was stolen from the king last week. Without it he cannot rule, and rival lords are already moving. Follow the thieves across the lands and recover it.
ending: The crown is recovered and the thieves are finished. The king keeps his throne, and he owes you.

steps.tell: The thieves hid a piece of the regalia in {area}. They thought nobody would look there. Search for it.
The thieves have a camp in {area}. Defeat them and take back what they stole.
Their trail leads to {area}. Go there and see who they work for.
There are too many guards in {area} to sneak past. Defeat them.
The crown itself is hidden in {area}. Search for it, and bring it home.

title: The Lost Courier
tagline: A sealed letter, three strangers and a message that must arrive.
opening: A letter was given to a courier, and the courier never arrived. Somebody, somewhere, is still waiting for it. Let us see who.
ending: The letter reached the hand it was meant for, and the world is a little less lost for it.

postmaster.name: Aldis the Postmaster
lines: No courier has come through in days. I fear the worst.
If you find the letter, do not open it.
after: You found the courier? Thank the stars. I will not send another on that road alone.
finished: The letter arrived! I have had word. You have the thanks of the whole post.

courier.name: Wren the Courier
lines: I ran. I am not proud of it, but I ran.
Take the letter. Take it to the one it was meant for.
after: I am no longer afraid of that road. Not with the letter in good hands.
finished: I ride again tomorrow. Perhaps I will tell the tale of the day strangers saved my route.

reader.name: Sage Orrin
lines: Letters from the old road. Rare, these days.
Whoever sent this knew more than they wrote.
after: I have read it twice now. It says more than I care to repeat.
finished: Come back one day. I will have a good deal more to tell you.

steps.tell: The postmaster in {area} is beside himself. Find Aldis, and hear what happened.
says: A courier left here three days ago with a sealed letter, and has not been seen since.
She was last bound for the lands beyond. Find her, if you can, and the letter with her.

steps.tell: Whatever stopped the courier is still out there in {area}. Clear the road before you follow it.
A frightened traveller is hiding in {area}. Find Wren the courier.
says: You came for the letter. Good. I could not carry it another step.
It is for the old sage who keeps the lore. Please, see it into their hands.

steps.tell: The sage the letter is for lives in {area}. Carry the Sealed Letter there and give it over.
says: Ah. So it has come at last. You have done more than you know.
What it says is not for you, but this I will tell you: the roads will be safer for it.

title: The Silent Bell
tagline: A bell that stopped ringing, a keeper with a secret, a trail to follow.
opening: There was a bell in the lands that rang every dusk. It has gone silent, and the silence has begun to spread.
ending: The bell rang again at dusk, and everyone who heard it knew the long silence was over.

ringer.name: Old Maren the Ringer
lines: Forty years I rang that bell. Now there is only quiet.
Find what took the clapper, and bring it home.
after: You have the clapper? Then there is hope for my bell yet.
finished: Did you hear it ring? Forty years, and I wept like a child. Thank you.

smith.name: Dorrin Ashhand
lines: I mend what breaks, but I cannot mend what is missing.
Bring me the clapper and the bell will sing.
after: It rings true now. Take care of it, and take care of each other.
finished: I heard the bell from here this dusk. It made the whole forge feel lighter.

steps.tell: The bell-ringer in {area} has a sorrow to tell. Find Old Maren.
says: The bell hangs there still, but its voice is gone. The clapper was taken in the night.
Whoever took it left tracks heading out. Follow them.

steps.tell: The tracks end in {area}. The clapper is hidden somewhere near. Search the land until you have it.
Whatever carried it off has made its den in {area}, and it will not give the clapper up without a fight.
Take the clapper to the smith in {area}. Find Dorrin Ashhand.
says: A fine piece, and nearly whole. Give me a moment at the anvil.
There. Carry it back to the bell, and may it ring true.

steps.tell: The bell hangs where it always did, in {area}. Return the clapper to it, and let it ring.

title: The Wanderer's Debt
tagline: A stranger owes a favour to someone he has never met, and you are the road between.
opening: A wanderer on the road owes a debt he cannot pay. Perhaps you can pay it for him, and learn something on the way.
ending: The debt is paid, the wanderer is free, and two strangers parted as friends.

wanderer.name: Corwin the Wanderer
lines: I owe someone a debt, and I do not even know their face.
They live beyond the next land, so I am told.
after: You have the coins? Then I am a free man, or near enough.
finished: The debt is paid, and I am lighter for it. Whatever road you take, I wish you a kinder one.

creditor.name: Keeper Hale
lines: A debt? I had forgotten it entirely.
Odd, to be repaid by strangers.
after: Odd to be repaid by strangers, but I will not refuse a good deed.
finished: Corwin sat at my fire last night. I did not know a debt could make a friend.

steps.tell: A traveller in {area} is looking for help with a debt. Find Corwin.
says: Take these coins, friends. They are what I owe, and a little more.
The one I owe lives some way off. Please, find them. I cannot.

steps.tell: On the road to the creditor, {area} offers what a gift ought to have beside it. Gather it as you pass.
The creditor is in {area}. Find Keeper Hale, and settle the debt.
says: These are the old coins, aren't they? My grandmother's pouch.
Tell Corwin the debt is paid, and something more besides. He is welcome at my fire.

title: The Innkeeper's Worry
tagline: A quiet inn, an empty room and a guest who left without paying or saying goodbye.
opening: The innkeeper has kept a room for a regular guest for twenty years. This season the guest never came, and the innkeeper cannot sleep for worrying.
ending: The old guest is found, well and only lost in grief. The room at the inn is aired, and a lamp burns in its window again.

innkeeper.name: Mother Brannagh
lines: Twenty years, and never once late. Something is wrong, I can feel it.
Sit, eat. Then go and look for him, if you would.
after: Any word? I keep his room aired, every morning.
finished: He is coming back for the winter. Your supper is on the house, tonight and every night.

pilgrim.name: Old Tobin
lines: Leave me be. I am only resting.
My wife walked this road with me every year. This year I walk it alone.
after: Tell Brannagh I am well. Tell her I will come when I can face the room.
finished: I went back to the inn. It was easier than I feared.

steps.tell: The innkeeper in {area} has a worry she will tell to anyone who sits a while. Find Mother Brannagh.
says: My oldest guest walks the far road every year, and every year he stays here. Not this year.
He always stops at the same places on the way. Start where the road leaves us.

steps.tell: The old guest always rested in {area} on his way. Walk there and look about for any sign of him.
A grey-bearded traveller sits alone in {area}, and has done for days. Find Old Tobin.
says: She found me, then. Brannagh always does.
Take this flower to her. She will know what it means, and why I am late.

steps.tell: Carry the Pressed Flower back to the inn in {area}, and tell Brannagh what you found.

title: Market Day
tagline: The big market is in three days, and half the stalls have nothing to sell.
opening: Market day is when the whole valley comes to town, and this year the stalls are bare. The merchants say the roads are bad. The townsfolk say the merchants are lazy. Somebody has to find out.
ending: Market day came, the stalls were full, and the town sang until dawn. The merchants have not stopped telling people who saved it.

merchant.name: Pella Quickcoin
lines: Bare stalls, and the market in three days. I will be ruined.
My goods are stuck somewhere on the road. I would pay well to know where.
after: Is that my wagon's mark? Then it is out there still.
finished: Best market in ten years. If you ever need anything, it is half price for you.

carter.name: Big Ansel
lines: A wheel broke, and then the ox wandered off. It has been a week like that.
I am not going anywhere until somebody helps me.
after: Off you go. I will have the wagon in town by market day, I promise.
finished: We made it with an hour to spare. I owe you a cart ride, any time.

smith.name: Hilde the Smith
lines: Broken wheel? Bring me the iron and I will mend it before supper.
Anything worth doing is worth a fair price.
after: There, a rim that will outlast the wagon. Take it to your carter.
finished: Market day, and my hammer has not stopped. Good for business, you lot.

steps.tell: A merchant in {area} is pacing beside an empty stall. Find Pella Quickcoin and hear her out.
says: My wagon left the far farms a week ago. It should have been here by now.
Follow the road out. If my carter is in a ditch, I want to know.

steps.tell: A big man is sitting beside a lopsided wagon in {area}. Find Big Ansel.
says: The wheel rim cracked clean through. I need a smith, and I cannot leave the goods.
Take the broken rim to a smith, and quick. Market day will not wait.

steps.tell: Carry the broken rim to the smith in {area}. Find Hilde.
says: Cracked by a stone, by the look of it. Give me a moment at the forge.
There. Run it back to your carter before the light goes.

steps.tell: While the wheel is fitted, Ansel asks for something to pack around the goods in {area}. Gather it, and the wagon can roll.

title: Stone and Steel
tagline: A gem in the pack is only a pebble until it is set in something.
opening: A stone that stays in a pack is a stone wasted. A smith knows better, and so, soon, will you.
ending: You set the stone, tried the edge and found it keen. The smith will tell the story for years, with a few embellishments of their own.

steps.tell: Set a gem in a good piece of gear, from the Inventory tab, and see what a little patience makes of it. {area} is as fine a place to do it as any.
A new piece wants trying. Take it into {area} and let something with opinions see what it can do.
Word of fine work travels faster than the worker. Show yours in {area}, where someone has already been asking after it.
